govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIReportCD-1_F: J. Edgar Hoover’s FBI Report CD-1 — his letter to J. Lee Rankin — is a Bureau file. Hoover fed the commission the Bureau’s findings. The letter shaped the probe. The declassified report is a primary source. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
cecilia-or-memoirs-of-an-heiress-volume-: Fanny Burney's celebrated 1782 novel introduces Cecilia Beverley, a young heiress whose fortune comes with a catch: her husband must take her family name. Fortune-hunters and fops swarm around her in fashionable London, testing her judgment and her heart. Witty, sharp-eyed, and full of social satire, the novel made Burney one of the most admired writers of her age.
a-political-and-social-history-of-modern: Historian Carlton Hayes opens his sweeping survey of modern Europe with this first volume, covering the continent's transformation from the old order to the modern age. Politics, society, and economics are woven together to explain how nations, empires, and revolutions made the Europe of the twentieth century. A classic college text, clear and richly detailed.
life-of-her-most-gracious-majesty-the-qu: Sarah Tytler opens her life of Queen Victoria with the princess's youth and early reign. Drawing on public records and personal knowledge, she presents the young queen with Victorian admiration. This first volume covers the girl who became the symbol of an age.
the-heart-of-mid-lothian-volume-1: Walter Scott's beloved novel opens with Jeanie Deans — the humble Scottish heroine whose walk to London to save her sister became legend. This first volume sets her extraordinary moral journey in motion through Edinburgh's streets and courts. Many consider it Scott's finest achievement.
old-mortality-volume-1: The first volume of Scott's Covenanter novel introduces Henry Morton and the religious wars of 1679 Scotland. Old Mortality himself — the wanderer who tends the martyrs' graves — gives the tale its haunting frame. Scott's historical imagination at its richest and most humane.
speeches-on-questions-of-public-policy-v: John Bright, the great Quaker orator, speaks on the public questions of Victorian England — free trade, parliamentary reform, and peace among nations. His plain, powerful eloquence moved multitudes and shaped policy. The voice of liberal England at its noblest and best.
the-land-of-midian-revisited-volume-1: Richard Burton returns to the Land of Midian — the Arabian wilderness of mines and mystery — in this first volume of his revisit. His bold, learned narrative blends exploration with deep Eastern lore. The great traveler in his element. Desert forts, ancient mines, and Bedouin camps fill this bold record of Arabian travel.
the-history-of-the-united-states-from-14: Julian Hawthorne, the romancer's son, opens his popular history of the United States with the age of discovery — Columbus, the conquistadors, and the first settlements. the-great-conspiracy-volume-1: General John Logan, the Union hero, opens his massive history of the Civil War with the roots of the conflict — slavery, secession, and the plot against the Union. His soldier's view is partisan but powerful. This first volume sets the stage for the great struggle.
the-prince-and-the-pauper-part-1: Mark Twain's beloved tale opens as Tom Canty, the pauper, trades places with Prince Edward in Tudor London.
